terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Not solved; review camera is fixed by the consumer harness.

objectClass.primaryType: small stack of three gouda-style cheese cubes
objectClass.notes: Matte faceted clay shading, flat color facets only. First box-primitive ingredient in this sub-batch; also the only one deviating from the flat-mound Y=0 cluster convention (a real physical stack instead).

reasoning: Three near-identical macro bodies differing only in XZ offset/yaw and the top instance's stacked Y, so componentCount scores 1.
Silhouette scores 2 (not 1): rounded-cube profile + hole depressions + the stack's own real elevation are more structurally involved than a smooth-taper lathe body.
hierarchyDepth scores 2: each cube has a real meso-level rind-face child (per-face material assignment), one level deeper than choco/cranberry's flat mesh=1 bodies.
materialLayerCount scores 1: 2 buckets needed (body + rind), matching olive/blueberry's precedent scale.
Local detail density scores 2: squircle rounding + front-face hole depressions are two distinct authored deformations.
Occlusion risk scores 1: the top cube's underside (resting on the lower cubes) is hidden but not identity-critical.
Action readiness scores 0: static turntable showcase prop.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Simple tier by part count, but needs meso depth (rind-face child) and material local overrides (2 dropped hex, each justified) like olive/blueberry, plus a documented placement-convention exception unique to this ingredient.

detailInventory.note: Enumerated by hand from the three supplied reference views -- CRIB.md skip rule for single-repeated-system objects.

details.observation: An entire cube face reads solid rust-orange, not a thin edge stripe.
details.inference: Wax-rind coating on one whole cut face of the cheese block.

details.observation: 2 cubes side by side + 1 physically resting on top, with real vertical elevation (not a flat-camera-angle illusion).
details.inference: A literal stack of cheese cubes, distinct from this batch's other flat-mound clusters.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

mustMatch: top cube physically supported, no floating gap

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Softly rounded/chamfered edges on every cube
Full rind face visible and distinct from body
Sunken holes visible on the front face
Top cube rests on the lower cubes, no floating gap

droppedPasses.lighting-pass: lighting is fixed by the consumer harness and is not authorable in the model
droppedPasses.interaction-pass: static showcase prop with no sockets, hinges or colliders beyond a bounding proxy

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: Consumer runtime keeps only map and color; repo bans PBR maps outright.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold

lightingPass.authority: Lighting is fixed by the consumer: scripts/breadlab.ts mirrors scripts/thumbsHarness.ts with a warm directional key 0xffe2b0 at (-2, 6, 2) intensity 1.4, an ambient 0xfff0dc at 0.75 and a cool fill 0xdce8ff at (2.5, 3, -2) intensity 0.2.
mustAvoid: relying on a contact shadow the harness does not render

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The runtime normalizes the stack's longest axis to 1.6, so absolute dimensions are arbitrary.
Exact hole size/position and stack nestling depth are not identity-critical at pixel precision; the rounded-cube silhouette + full rind face + physical stacking read is what the review scores.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z, the direction the harness three-quarter camera at (-1.6, 2.2, 2.6) looks from
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: CUBE_HALF = 0.5 relative unit. Absolute scale is meaningless: the consumer runtime refits the cluster's longest axis to 1.6 (types.ts section 6).

silhouette.boundingShape: 3-cube physical stack, roughly 2.16 wide by 2.0 tall by 1.2 deep in relative units
silhouette.symmetry: each cube is bilaterally symmetric before the front-face hole depressions and rind-face assignment; the stack as a whole is asymmetric
dominantCurves: softly rounded/chamfered edges on every face boundary
negativeSpaces: 2 sunken circular holes per cube on the front face
contact seam where the top cube rests on the two lower cubes
landmarks: one full rind face per cube, always oriented outward/visible in the placement

observations: 3 cubes with pronounced rounded/chamfered edges, 2 resting side by side + 1 physically stacked on top
every cube shows one ENTIRE side face solid rust-orange (rind) -- not a thin edge stripe
every cube shows 2 sunken circular holes (one larger, one smaller) on its front-facing face
edges are visibly beveled on every face, not sharp 90-degree corners
holes read as darker circular depressions, no separate bright/dark ring color
3 roughly square footprints, top cube's footprint overlapping the gap between the 2 bottom cubes
rind face visible as a bright orange sliver along one edge from directly above

componentTree.name: Cheese Cube Stack
componentTree.topologyRationale: Transform-only assembly node carrying the three cube bodies; emits no geometry of its own.

collider.notes: Box bounding proxy; sufficient for a static showcase prop.

colorMaterialRecipe.materialClassRationale: Matte faceted ingredient prop, roughness 1.0, no specular lobe -- prompt JSON explicitly excludes shine.

localFeatures.name: Three-cube physical stack
localFeatures.description: Two cubes side by side on the ground + one physically resting on top of both (types.ts R1's spirit -- no unsupported floating parts -- but NOT the flat-mound-at-Y=0 convention the round/organic ingredients use; see spec risk stack-not-flat-mound).

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: faceted planar shading from split vertices
surfaceDetail.displacementPattern: squircle corner-rounding (sdRoundBox surface-point formula) + 2 vertex-depression holes on the front face, zero extra triangles
surfaceDetail.occlusionPattern: none -- runtime Lambert has no AO channel; per-face brightness comes from N.L falloff on each flat face's own normal
surfaceDetail.notes: Assembly node; no surface of its own.

componentTree.name: Cheese cube body (bottom-a)
componentTree.topologyRationale: A custom 6-face grid shell with a per-vertex squircle rounding transform (not THREE.BoxGeometry -- needs rounded edges + per-sector hole depressions no built-in primitive supports). One continuous watertight shell (coincident edge/corner vertices from adjacent faces map identically since rounding is a pure function of position), not an assembled-solid of 6 separate planes.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: low-poly prop, faceted after generation, no jitter (R4 exception -- reference shows completely clean flat faces, no organic noise anywhere)

deformationStack.notes: sdRoundBox surface-point formula: inner=half-0.13, clamp to inner box then push out by 0.13 along the clamp-delta direction. Flat face interiors pass through unchanged; only vertices within 0.13 of an edge/corner move.

2 interior grid vertices on the +Z face pulled inward along -Z: big hole at grid (1, 2) depth 0.09, small hole at grid (2, 1) depth 0.0675. Same body material -- no separate hole color (cracker.ts precedent).

geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: flat normals baked by splitting vertices (facet), never a flatShading flag. No jitter applied (R4 exception).

collider.notes: Box bounding proxy; sufficient for a static showcase prop.

colorMaterialRecipe.materialClassRationale: Matte faceted ingredient prop, roughness 1.0, no specular lobe -- prompt JSON explicitly excludes shine.
colorMaterialRecipe.zone: 5 of 6 faces (all but the rind face)

seams.notes: The rind face (+X) is a distinct per-face triangle group assigned to the cheese-rind material at build time -- known statically (which face is which), not a mask or slice. Watertight because rounding is a pure function of vertex position, so no seam gap opens at the rind/body edge.

localFeatures.name: Softly rounded/chamfered edges
localFeatures.description: Squircle rounding on every edge/corner, ~26% of half-extent -- distinctly soft, not a sharp 90-degree cube.

localFeatures.name: Two sunken circular holes
localFeatures.description: One larger + one smaller vertex-depression dimple on the front face, same body material, read via facet-normal shading alone.

materials.name: Cheese body (butter-yellow)
materials.shaderModel: MeshStandardMaterial carrier; the consumer runtime swaps it for MeshLambertMaterial keeping only map and color

albedo.samplingNotes: Hand-transcribed from assets/prompts/ingredients/cheese.json geometry.surface, not pixel-sampled.

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: No texture is emitted. UVs exist only for merge attribute consistency.

roughness.localResponse: inert -- the runtime Lambert swap discards roughness entirely

ambientOcclusion.notes: No AO channel: the runtime Lambert material has none.

localOverrides.name: Per-face key-light shading
localOverrides.description: No second darker bucket is authored for the shaded-faces hex (#C9903A); a flat cube's own faces already read at different brightness depending on their normal direction under the runtime Lambert key light -- exactly what this hex describes.

localOverrides.name: Sunken holes read via facet shading only
localOverrides.description: No separate hole-color bucket (#D8A448) is authored; the depression's own facet normals darken under the key light (cracker.ts docking-hole precedent).

shaderNotes: Emit via scripts/breads/lib.ts stdMaterial(): MeshStandardMaterial with roughness 1, metalness 0.
Never set vertexColors: the runtime rebuilds every material as MeshLambertMaterial({map, color}).
Never set flatShading: that flag is not inherited by the runtime swap either. Faceting must be baked as split vertices.
materials.notes: 5 of 6 faces. Two solid colors for the whole cluster (types.ts inherited section 9); shaded-face hex and hole-color hex are both dropped (free via per-face N.L / cracker precedent).

repetitionSystems.name: Three-cube physical stack
repetitionSystems.elementKind: repeated macro body, each with its own body+rind child pair

distribution.mode: 2 hand-placed ground cubes + 1 physically stacked cube (bbox-floor-on-top-of-lower-group, not Y=0)

acceptance: Silhouette reads correctly without materials.
Quality contract has named all required macro feature groups before code generation.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

featureReviews.notes: 2 cubes side by side + 1 physically resting on top, well-supported (Box3-computed floor, zero gap); matches cheese.png's stack arrangement closely.
Squircle rounding (radius 0.1, ~20% of half-extent) reads as a distinct soft bevel on every edge/corner across all orbit angles, not a sharp 90-degree cube.

Full -X face reads as a solid dark rust-orange rind on every cube, oriented toward the hero camera. Repositioned from +X to -X after cmp-1 showed it facing away from the default camera (documented in code comments).

2x2-vertex-block dimples on the front face, tuned to a shallow depth (0.038/0.028) after an isolation test (shot-isolation-debug.png) proved deeper holes (0.07/0.05) caused a jagged facet artifact at this low grid resolution. Now reads as a subtle but present darker patch pair, not a crisp circular hole -- an accepted tradeoff (important tier, not mustPass) between hole readability and surface cleanliness at this budget.
Top cube's own Box3 floor is set exactly to the two lower cubes' combined Box3.max.y (computed at build time, not hardcoded) -- zero gap on all orbit angles, no floating.

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Own-vision read across cmp-1/2/3 plus 6 follow-up debug renders (rind orientation, hole spacing, T-junction hypothesis test, isolation test, shallow/mid depth tuning): the jagged artifact traced conclusively (isolation test) to hole-depression depth, not rounding or grid-density mismatch; final depth (0.038/0.028) balances hole readability against surface cleanliness within the cluster tri/KB budget.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Hard consumer budget for the 'cluster' ingredient group: <=700 tri and <=68KB target (types.ts R2), hard ceiling <=2500 tri and <=100KB. Target reached by construction (6 faces x 4x4 quads/face x 3 cubes = 576 tri; rounding + hole depressions add zero triangles), not by decimation.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Warm directional key 0xffe2b0 at (-2, 6, 2), intensity 1.4, upper-left.
lightingFromPhoto.exposure: no exposure control, no tone mapping.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Ambient 0xfff0dc at 0.75 -- each cube face's own brightness comes from its normal's angle to the key light, giving the 'shaded faces' effect for free.

proceduralStrategy: Build each cube as 6 independent per-face grids (SEGMENTS_PER_AXIS quads/edge), right-handed (U,V,N) triples per face for consistent outward winding.

Apply the squircle rounding transform (sdRoundBox surface-point formula) to every vertex -- a pure function of position, so coincident edge/corner vertices from adjacent faces map identically without a shared index.
Depress 2 interior grid vertices on the +Z face along -Z for the front-face holes.
No jitter (R4 exception -- reference shows clean flat faces). Bake faceting by splitting vertices (facet); never request flatShading.
Assign the +X face's triangles to the rind material, the other 5 faces to the body material -- known statically per face, not a mask or slice.
Project top-planar UVs per face bucket, then merge all three cubes by material into exactly two meshes.

Place the two ground cubes with their own bbox floor at world Y=0; compute the top cube's Y from the two lower cubes' combined Box3 max.y (a deliberate exception to the flat-mound R1 convention, see spec risk stack-not-flat-mound).
animationAnchors: root pivot supports whole-stack rotation for the showcase turntable
each cube is a named instance
destructionAnchors: each cube is its own fractureGroup; the only plausible break is the top cube toppling off the stack

risks.description: assets/prompts/ingredients/cheese.json describes the rind as 'a thin warm wax rind along one edge', but the actual reference render shows an entire solid-colored face.
risks.mitigation: Image is shape/color-region authority per INGREDIENTS.md; the rind is authored as one whole face (+X), matching the reference directly rather than the undersold prompt text.

risks.description: The shaded-faces hex (#C9903A) is not painted as a separate bucket.
risks.mitigation: A flat cube's own faces already shade differently by normal direction under the runtime key light -- exactly this hex's effect, achieved for free via geometry+lighting.

risks.description: The hole hex (#D8A448) is not painted as a separate bucket.
risks.mitigation: Holes are pure vertex-depression dimples in the body material (cracker.ts precedent); their own facet-normal shading gives the darkened read.

risks.description: The top cube's bbox floor is NOT at world Y=0, unlike every other cluster ingredient in this batch (olive/choco/cranberry/blueberry all keep every instance on the shared ground per R1).
risks.mitigation: A cube stack's flat top/bottom edges make true physical elevation visually unmistakable -- a camera-angle illusion (used by the round/organic ingredients) cannot fake a flat cube resting on another flat cube. The top cube IS fully supported (zero gap, computed from the lower cubes' own Box3), satisfying R1's actual intent (no floating/unsupported parts) even though it deviates from the flat-mound convention.

risks.description: Any vertex-color-based region paint is silently discarded by the runtime's MeshLambertMaterial swap.
risks.mitigation: The body/rind split is carried by two separate materials on two separate per-face triangle groups, assigned statically at build time. No vertexPaint block is authored anywhere in this spec.

risks.description: A flatShading flag is not inherited by the runtime material swap.
risks.mitigation: Faceting is baked into geometry by splitting vertices (scripts/breads/lib.ts facet) before export.

risks.description: If jitter were applied to this 6-independent-face (non-welded) topology, coincident edge/corner vertices from adjacent faces would move independently and open a crack.
risks.mitigation: Jitter is deliberately omitted for cheese (R4 exception, also matches the reference's clean unjittered look) -- the squircle rounding stays watertight because it is a pure function of vertex position, safe without a shared index.
